1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Doldari for three days. Kim Haneul's older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and since then Haneul had been running the village's small apothecary alone.
When night fell, she shut the outer door, counted the day's earnings, extinguished the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when urgent knocking sounded at the door below, followed by a man's voice. "Is anyone there?"
A young man stood at the door, soaked to the bone. The cloth wrapped around his left arm was stained with blood. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was with the Azure Dragon Society.
"Please treat my wound," Park Junho said in a low voice. "I will pay you. Will three thousand five hundred nyang be enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oiled paper from inside his coat. "This letter must be delivered to Cheongpungsa by the eighteenth of the fifth month."
Haneul thought to herself. The neighbors had been jealous that the apothecary was doing well, and now a strange man had shown up in the middle of the night.
Still, Haneul refused the money and simply said, "I'll guide you to the mountain early tomorrow morning."
2: As soon as day broke, the two set out. Haneul carried a basket on her back; inside were rice balls, medicinal herbs, and a worn umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain they met Lee Youngsoo, an old man chopping firewood. He set down his axe and lowered his voice. Three strangers had been asking around the village entrance the previous evening, looking for a young injured man.
"Haneul, take the side path," Lee Youngsoo said. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul took the lead, planting each step firmly as she went. Park Junho followed silently behind her.

By noon the rain had stopped and the mountain mist slowly lifted, revealing the roof of Cheongpungsa in the distance. A nun stood at the temple gate. It was Jeonghye, who greeted guests at the temple.
Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for two years."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "You saved my life." Haneul smiled and replied, "Then next time you come, fix the roof of the medicine shop." Park Junho stayed at the temple.
Toward evening Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home it was already dark. She lit the oil lamp and sat behind the counter for a long while.
